name: Colobomatous Microphthalmia Heart Disease Hearing Loss Syndrome
aliases: Colobomatous Microphthalmia with Congenital Heart Defects and Sensorineural Hearing Loss
Syndromic Colobomatous Microphthalmia with Cardiac and Auditory Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of colobomatous microphthalmia confirmed by ophthalmologic examination
Structural congenital heart defects identified by echocardiography or cardiac imaging
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Family history suggestive of autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes if available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: colobomatous microphthalmia, congenital heart disease, and sensorineural hearing loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may aid but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic ocular malformation involving incomplete closure of the optic fissure
Includes septal defects, valve anomalies, or complex congenital heart malformations
Typically moderate to severe hearing impairment detected early in life
searchTerms: hearing loss from nerve damage both ears

common.notes: Smaller than normal corneal diameter often accompanying microphthalmia
Mild to moderate delay in achieving developmental milestones

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy
common.notes: Signs such as tachypnea, poor feeding, and failure to thrive
Arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities may be present
Underdevelopment of the optic nerve contributing to visual impairment

occasional.notes: Progressive worsening of hearing loss over time
Subtle craniofacial anomalies such as broad nasal bridge or micrognathia
Decreased muscle tone observed in infancy

rare.notes: Rarely associated with structural kidney abnormalities
Uncommon skin findings such as hemangiomas
Rare reports of thyroid or adrenal abnormalities

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers identified
imaging: Ocular ultrasound or MRI showing coloboma and microphthalmia
Brain MRI may show optic nerve hypoplasia
genetic: Possible pathogenic variants in genes involved in ocular and cardiac development (e.g., PAX6, CHD7) though no single gene definitively established
other: Audiometric testing confirming bilateral sensorineural hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive optic atrophy rather than coloboma

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects causing cyanosis or heart failure
Profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss detected in infancy
Marked visual impairment due to extensive coloboma or microphthalmia
